production: Original deterministic material-inspired synthesis; no real recordings, AI model calls, downloaded samples or new dependencies.
runtimeIntegration: Offline listening revision only; game audio and previous studies preserved.
listeningAcceptance: Pending user audition; energy and periodicity metrics are not perceptual quality scores.

physical.userPreference: 2026-11-16: more realistic and restrained; shorter physical contact, limited low end, no exaggerated critical/kill accents.
physical.provenance: Original deterministic NumPy/SciPy material modelling; no recorded foley, AI audio, external samples, or listening approval claimed.
physical.sourceChange: V2 sinusoidal drum/body chirps, pitched steel sweeps, and sustained comb-string sound are replaced by finite noise excitation through damped physical-mode banks and irregular friction grains.
physical.mixing: Each layer is calibrated with RMS over a local active window. Layer ratios, microtiming, damping and excitation vary independently; no per-cue full-peak loudness normalisation.
physical.war: Air is separate; contact combines 1-15ms cut, 12-45ms cloth/body compression, and strongly damped inharmonic steel. Heavy is modestly thicker, never a bass drum.
physical.bow: Draw is quieter than release; string/bow-limb ringing is intentionally brief. Heavy preserves a puncture before its wood/body layer and avoids gunshot-like blast.
physical.acceptance: Synthesis and numerical checks only. Aesthetic acceptance requires user audition and device playback.

elemental.direction: More realistic and restrained; small-scale combustion and dry electric arcs, not ultimate-sized impacts.
elemental.provenance: Original deterministic NumPy/SciPy synthesis; no recordings, soundfonts, AI calls or downloads.

fire.transient: A tiny ignition crack and a short band-limited bipolar pressure pulse.
fire.body: Independent breath-shaped turbulent packets with irregular spacing and changing bandwidth; no continuous white-noise bed.
fire.tail: The combustion expands over 0.1–0.3 seconds, then small embers become sparse and disappear.
fire.removedFromV2: Continuous low-frequency noise, regular 23/37Hz flutter and a descending sub-bass sine body.

lightning.transient: A short broadband arc fracture with a compact, rapidly damped structure contact.
lightning.body: A few milliseconds of low-mid resonant energy rather than sustained pitched synthesis.
lightning.tail: Mostly silence, interrupted by a small number of much quieter branch arcs.
lightning.removedFromV2: 360–2100Hz ascending oscillator, 2.31x tonal partial and sawtooth amplitude modulation; long high hiss and rumble.

elemental.timing: All six durations match v2 exactly so the existing 15-second demonstrations retain their segment boundaries.
elemental.variants: Deterministic variations alter packet timing, turbulent excitation, damping and small pressure differences; no large pitch transposition.
elemental.mix: Peak headroom cap 0.58; no independent loudness normalization that would magnify quiet tails.
elemental.acceptance: Technical measures can verify finite samples and bounded peaks; realism, restraint and impact need human audition.

comparison.crossProfessionLoudness: Each before/after pair has its own feasible target; these are not final gameplay mix balances.
comparison.cueSchedule: Main contact onsets and sections inherited from v2; decorative doubles are muted in v3.
comparison.loudnessReference: Uncompressed PCM WAV. Lossy previews can shift gated LUFS for sparse transients; use the WAV A/B for level comparison.
